title: Ramayana Closes Day 20 at ₹972.95 Crore Net, ₹27 Crore From ₹1,000 Crore Club
excerpt: The Nitesh Tiwari epic earned ₹17.50 crore on its third Tuesday and stands at ₹1,735.15 crore worldwide, set to become only the fourth Indian film to collect ₹1,000 crore net in India.
body:
• Ramayana: Part 1 closed Day 20 (Tuesday, November 24) at ₹972.95 crore net in India — ₹27.05 crore short of the ₹1,000 crore India net mark, according to Sacnilk.
  • The film earned ₹17.50 crore net on Day 20, a rise from Monday, across 15,817 shows at 28.1% occupancy; the Hindi version contributed ₹14.25 crore, over 81% of the day.
  • Worldwide gross stood at ₹1,735.15 crore after 20 days, including ₹573 crore from overseas, according to Sacnilk figures reported by Daily Jagran.
  • If it crosses ₹1,000 crore net in India, Ramayana will be only the fourth Indian film to do so, after Baahubali 2, Pushpa 2 and Dhurandhar 2.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1 is within one strong day of a mark only three Indian films have ever reached. The mythological epic, in Hindi with Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil and Telugu versions, closed its 20th day on Tuesday, November 24 at ₹972.95 crore net in India (₹1,162.15 crore gross), according to trade tracker Sacnilk — ₹27.05 crore short of ₹1,000 crore net from Indian theatres alone.

Day 20 itself moved the film closer: it earned ₹17.50 crore net, up from ₹12.70 crore on Monday, across 15,817 shows with 28.1% occupancy, Daily Jagran reported, citing Sacnilk. The Hindi version brought in ₹14.25 crore — over 81% of the day's earnings — with Malayalam adding ₹1.25 crore, Kannada ₹90 lakh and Telugu ₹40 lakh. Overseas, the film added ₹5 crore on Day 20, taking its international gross to ₹573 crore and its worldwide gross to ₹1,735.15 crore.

The club it is about to join

For nearly seven years, Baahubali 2 remained the only Indian film to have collected ₹1,000 crore net at the domestic box office before Pushpa 2 joined the club in December 2024, Sacnilk noted. Dhurandhar 2 became the first Bollywood film to achieve the milestone earlier this year. If Ramayana crosses the line in the next few days, it will be only the fourth Indian film to do so — and, Sacnilk noted, the second Bollywood film after Dhurandhar 2.

The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, with Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, Sunny Deol as Hanuman, Arun Govil as King Dasharath and Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi. It is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios, in association with DNEG and Monster Mind Creations, and released in theatres on November 5, 2026. Malhotra has said the two Ramayana films together will cost about $500 million — over ₹4,000 crore — according to Daily Jagran.

What to watch

The near-term question is timing, not direction: at Day 20's ₹17.50 crore pace, the ₹1,000 crore net line is a matter of days, and Sacnilk's live Day 21 tracking had already taken the India net past ₹977 crore part-way through Wednesday. For diaspora audiences, the overseas figure is the other half of the story — ₹573 crore of the worldwide total has come from outside India, a share that underlines how much of this film's record run is being powered by audiences abroad as well as at home.
